# Troubleshooting FAQ

<!-- Generated by tools/generate-codkit-docs.mjs; do not edit by hand. -->

This page is keyed from the live registry in [`packages/codkit/src/lib/messages.ts`](../../../packages/codkit/src/lib/messages.ts). It covers every currently registered error and warning code. The hint printed for the specific failure is authoritative; the table gives the usual operator path.

## How should automation read a failure?

Use `--json` and branch on `exitCode` plus `errors[].code`. Exit 1 is a red check/result, exit 2 is usage/environment/startup, and exit 3 is a required human decision. A CLI typo occurs before a command context exists: it prints codeless `error:`/`hint:` lines to stderr, exits 2, and does not emit a JSON envelope.

## Error codes

| Code | What it means | Typical next action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `CK-E-CONFIG` | Configuration or a command value is invalid or missing. | Read the emitted hint; restore/repair the named config or use the exact usage it prints. |
| `CK-E-NOT-A-REPO` | The resolved fork path is not a usable Git work tree. | Check `codkit where`, then point `--fork-dir`/`CODKIT_FORK_DIR` at the supplied checkout or run `codkit clone` outside CI. |
| `CK-E-NOT-UPSTREAM` | The tree does not contain the configured upstream anchor. | Supply the correct fork repository; do not repurpose an unrelated checkout. |
| `CK-E-PIN-UNREACHABLE` | The configured pin/ref is absent or outside the expected upstream history. | Fetch/provide that object outside Codkit CI, then rerun `codkit check-tree`; Codkit does not fetch it implicitly. |
| `CK-E-LFS` | Git LFS support or required LFS content is missing. | Install Git LFS and populate LFS objects outside `--ci`, or include them in the offline fork-tree supply. |
| `CK-E-LOCKED` | Another Codkit operation owns the per-tree lock. | Wait for the named process; if it is gone, follow the stale-lock hint instead of deleting active state blindly. |
| `CK-E-DIRTY-TREE` | Unextracted or otherwise disallowed work makes the requested transition unsafe. | Run `codkit status`, then `codkit save` for work to keep or restore it deliberately. Fork-tree commits can also be dropped on purpose with `codkit load --discard` (they stay reachable under `refs/codkit/consumed/`, where `codkit gc` eventually spends them; the flag is refused under `--ci`). A tracked upstream file a build rewrote is dropped by name with `codkit load --fresh --discard`, which announces every path it drops and never touches a file carrying a marker block - extract that one with `codkit save`, or move the edit out of the file. A tree left by `overlay apply` returns to dev mode with `codkit load --fresh` (only the exact overlay materialization is replaced). CI should receive a disposable clean tree. |
| `CK-E-TREE-READONLY` | Codkit cannot write the fork tree or its required runtime state. | Fix ownership/permissions and rerun. The patchset source may be read-only only when `.codkit` is supplied as a separate writable mount; the fork tree itself must be writable for `ci`. |
| `CK-E-CRLF` | A patchable text target contains carriage returns. | Normalize the intended file to LF without changing unrelated bytes, then save again. |
| `CK-E-EOF-NEWLINE` | A file that had a final newline at the pin lost it. | Restore the final LF and rerun the command. |
| `CK-E-ENCODING` | Patch input is binary or not valid UTF-8. | Use the resource layer for binary content or restore valid UTF-8 for text. |
| `CK-E-MARKER-MALFORMED` | A marker line has invalid syntax. | Repair the exact named line to the configured form; use `codkit marker new` for new blocks. |
| `CK-E-MARKER-NESTED` | A marker begins inside another marker. | Separate the interventions into non-nested blocks. |
| `CK-E-MARKER-UNBALANCED` | Begin/end marker IDs do not pair. | Make the closing ID match its opening block. |
| `CK-E-MARKER-UNCLOSED` | A marker block has no closing line. | Add the configured end marker for the same ID. |
| `CK-E-MARKER-DUP-ID` | An intervention ID is reused. | Assign a fresh ID matching `idPattern`; IDs are unique across layers/artifacts. |
| `CK-E-MARKER-BAD-ID` | A marker ID violates the configured pattern. | Choose a configured subsystem and three-digit suffix shown in the conventions reference. |
| `CK-E-HUNK-OUTSIDE-MARKER` | A patch hunk changes content outside its marker block. | Move the intended edit into the block or choose another layer; do not widen the patch silently. |
| `CK-E-DELETES-UPSTREAM-LINE` | A patch removes an upstream line. | Preserve/comment the upstream line and express the behavior inside a marker or higher layer. |
| `CK-E-DELETES-UPSTREAM-FILE` | A patch removes an upstream file. | Use the hide/removed mechanism with its guard instead of a deletion patch. |
| `CK-E-NEW-FILE-IN-UPSTREAM-ZONE` | A new file appeared outside own code without explicit authorization. | Prefer `delta/own`; only when the path is inherently upstream-shaped, rerun save with repeatable `--allow-new-file <path>`. |
| `CK-E-HEADER-MISSING` | A new patch has no pending metadata header. | Scaffold with `codkit marker new`, complete its metadata, then run `codkit save`. |
| `CK-E-FORBIDDEN-TARGET` | The selected path cannot carry this patch/marker operation. | Follow the emitted layer/path hint; binary, own, protected, and unsupported-extension targets need another mechanism. |
| `CK-E-MARKER-ARTIFACT-MISMATCH` | Tree markers, pending metadata, and patch artifacts disagree. | Inspect the named pair and use the normal marker/save transaction to restore one-to-one ownership. |
| `CK-E-UNTRACKED-INTERVENTION` | A change is not represented by a known delta artifact. | Extract it with `codkit save` or remove/restore the unintended tree edit. |
| `CK-E-STALE-ARTIFACT` | An artifact no longer has a valid current target/effect. | Review the upstream change; reresolve, retarget, or remove the intervention through the upgrade procedure. |
| `CK-E-OWN-UNCOVERED` | An own file is missing inventory/manifest coverage. | Declare it in the own manifest/entry structure named by the hint, then verify. |
| `CK-E-OWNER-UNKNOWN` | Metadata names an owner absent from `delta/owners.json`. | Use an existing owner key or add the team-owned mapping deliberately. |
| `CK-E-GUARD-MISSING` | An intervention that requires a contract guard has none or names an undeclared guard. | Add/declare the required own guard test and rerun `codkit verify`. |
| `CK-E-FORBIDDEN-SERVICE` | Own code overrides a configured bootstrap service. | Do not override that decorator; choose a supported seam or escalate the design. |
| `CK-E-OVERLAY-SCHEMA` | An overlay is syntactically/schema invalid or writes outside the allowed target policy. | Repair the named overlay operation; for non-product `package.json`, only script additions are allowed. |
| `CK-E-OVERLAY-DRIFT` | An overlay expectation or materialized target no longer matches the pin. | Review upstream, update the overlay expectation intentionally, and use `overlay check/apply`; do not hand-edit the target. |
| `CK-E-RULE-DRIFT` | A rewrite rule matched a different count/content than declared. | Review upstream and update or replace the rule; never weaken the expected count merely to get green. |
| `CK-E-ARTIFACT-BROKEN` | A delta/cycle artifact cannot be parsed, replayed, or trusted. | Repair the named source or resume its durable transaction; do not edit transaction state files unless the hint explicitly says so. |
| `CK-E-NET-FORBIDDEN` | The requested action would cross the active no-network boundary. | Provide the clone/ref/LFS object through the CI or supply kit, or run the explicitly networked command outside `--ci`. |
| `CK-E-LOG-INCOMPLETE` | An upgrade-cycle journal/history record is incomplete or inconsistent. | Complete the required record through `codkit cycle` before continuing. |
| `CK-E-BOTH-SIDES-EDITED` | The same file changed on both sides of the two repositories and needs a human decision. | For a `codkit sync` conflict the 3-way is already in the fork-tree file as diff3 markers: keep both sides and the block ids, then `codkit sync --continue` (`codkit sync --abort` returns everything to the state before the run; while markers remain, `--continue` refuses naming the file). For own code and mixed `--discard` runs there are no blocks to materialize into - pick a side by hand as the printed recipe says. |
| `CK-E-WORKTREE-REF-SHARED` | The generated branch is checked out in another worktree of the same repository, and moving it here would leave that worktree dirty. | Let the named worktree use its own branch (git -C <path> switch --detach) or remove it (git worktree remove <path>), then re-run; nothing was changed. |
| `CK-E-TREE-HEAD` | HEAD of the fork tree is off the generated branch while carrying commits that are not in patchset, or the line below the generated tip was rewritten. | Return HEAD to the generated branch (git switch codkit/applied/<tag>) or merge the commits there, then run codkit save; for a rewritten line reset the branch to the named generated tip or restore it from refs/codkit/consumed/. |
| `CK-E-PATCHSET-MOVED` | The patch set moved under a fork tree loaded from an older state: an artifact was edited or the patchset branch was switched between the load and the save. | Follow the printed manual merge recipe: return the delta to the loaded state (`git stash`, `git switch <branch>`, or `git checkout <sha> -- delta/`), run `codkit save`, bring the shift back (`git stash pop`, `git merge`, or `git rebase`), then `codkit load` - or let `codkit sync` perform all four in one command. Switching branches deliberately starts with a full `codkit save`, not a switch. |
| `CK-E-SYNC-IN-PROGRESS` | A two-way `codkit sync` left its transaction record behind without finishing, so the fork tree and the patch set are half one state and half another - or the abort found commits above the record that were not made by that run. | Wait for the running sync; otherwise resolve the record: resolve the conflict markers and `codkit sync --continue`, or `codkit sync --abort` to return everything to the state before the run. An abort that names foreign commits refuses on purpose - move or remove them by hand first. The record at `.codkit/sync-transaction.json` carries the pre-run heads and byte snapshots; do not delete it blind. |
| `CK-E-INTERNAL` | An unexpected Codkit failure escaped domain diagnosis. | Rerun with `--verbose` and attach the complete output to a bug report. |
| `CK-E-DEPS-MISSING` | Required runtime dependencies or their npm cache receipts are absent. | Install/restore Codkit dependencies in the tool root; for `ci --profile build`, also supply every dependency root the project type names (the message lists the missing `.package-lock.json` receipts) through the air-gapped cache/mount. The patch set is not the tool installation, and empty bind-mount directories do not count as restored caches. |
| `CK-E-LICENSE-HEADER` | A file of the standards package has no licence carrier, or a wrong one: no copyright line, no year on an own file, no `SPDX-License-Identifier`, an identifier that is not SPDX, an own file under a licence other than `UPL-1.0`, a binary or JSON without its `.license` sidecar, or a sidecar without its file. | Run `codkit license annotate` for the file, or fix the header (or the sidecar) as PROP-014 sec. 2 shows, within the first 20 non-empty lines; an own file carries exactly `UPL-1.0`. |
| `CK-E-LICENSE-THIRD-PARTY` | A file whose holder is not in the policy breaks the third-party rules: no `REUSE.toml` annotation covers it (a typo in the holder, or an undeclared third-party file), its licence is outside the allowlist or is `LicenseRef-*`/`NOASSERTION`, the carrier and the annotation disagree, or `THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md` is missing or stale. | Declare the file with `codkit license annotate --third-party --holder <name> --license <SPDX-ID> --source <where it came from>` (or fix the holder typo), keep the carrier and the annotation on the same licence, put the licence text in `LICENSES/`, then run `codkit license notices`. |
| `CK-E-LICENSE-PACKAGE` | The package as a whole is inconsistent: the manifest `license` field is not `UPL-1.0`, `LICENSE` or `LICENSES/UPL-1.0.txt` differs from the canonical UPL text, a licence in use has no `LICENSES/<ID>.txt` or `LICENSES/` carries a text nobody uses, `REUSE.toml` does not parse, a notices file exists without third-party files, or a symlink sits inside the package. | Restore the canonical files from the shipped package (never edit a licence text), add the missing `LICENSES/<ID>.txt` verbatim from SPDX or remove the unused one, fix `REUSE.toml`, remove the symlink; rerun `codkit license check <dir>`. |
| `CK-E-STANDARDS-DRIFT` | An installed copy under `vibevm/vibepacks/org.vibevm.codkit/` differs from the package codkit ships: a file was modified, added or removed. The same code covers an edited `LICENSE-CODKIT.md` copy. | The copy is codkit-owned. Run `codkit standards load --upgrade` to take the shipped copy (an edition may be extended in place under the same version), or move local edits into your own specs as a recorded deviation, delete the copy directory and run `codkit standards load` again; for an edited notice copy, delete the copy. Run `vibe install --offline` (after an upgrade `--force`) afterwards. |
| `CK-E-RUNTIME-DRIFT` | The installed copy of the codkit runtime library under `delta/own/codkit/` differs from the library codkit ships: a file was edited, added or removed, or an older version is installed. | The library is codkit-owned. Change it in codkit, not in the product; to take the shipped version run `codkit runtime load --upgrade`, which replaces the directory as a whole and lists what it replaced. |
| `CK-E-RUNTIME-PACKAGE` | The codkit installation carries no usable runtime library: `runtime/` of the installation has zero or several version directories, or the `CODKIT_RUNTIME_VERSION` literal in `common/version.ts` disagrees with the directory name. | Restore the codkit installation from the approved supply; nothing in the product repository is wrong. |
| `CK-E-DELIVERED-EDIT` | `codkit save` found a file under `src/vs/<own>/codkit/` in the fork tree that differs from `delta/own/codkit/`: a file delivered by codkit was edited in the tree. | Nothing was mirrored. Revert the edit in the tree, or make the change in codkit and run `codkit runtime load --upgrade`. |
| `CK-E-OWN-UNDER-CODKIT` | A unit in `patchset.delta.json` roots a path under `codkit/`, which is reserved for files codkit delivers and licenses. | Move the unit to another own path; `codkit/` belongs to codkit and the licence notice describes it as such. |
| `CK-E-HOOK-TOO-LARGE` | A patch declared `type = hook` carries more than three lines of code between its markers, or none of its lines imports or calls own code. | A hook is a graft: keep one import or one call that delegates into own code and move the logic into the own layer. |
| `CK-E-GEN-EXISTS` | `codkit gen` would overwrite a file that already exists under `delta/own/`. | Nothing was written. Remove or rename the existing file, or pick another feature id. |
| `CK-E-GEN-ID` | The feature id passed to `codkit gen feature` is not two or more dot-separated camelCase segments (for example `acme.smartPaste`). | Use a product prefix followed by camelCase segments; the first segment names the product. |
| `CK-E-OWN-EXTENSION-MANIFEST` | The `extensions` section of `delta/own/patchset.delta.json` does not describe a materializable extension: the `name` is not of the form `[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*`, two records claim one name, `delta/own-extensions/<name>/package.json` is missing, a directory under `delta/own-extensions/` is declared by no record, or the name collides with an extension the pin already ships. | Fix the record named by the finding: rename the extension, add the `package.json` the upstream build looks for, declare the directory, or remove it. Nothing was materialized. |
| `CK-E-OWN-EXTENSION-DRIFT` | A file under `extensions/<name>/` in the fork tree differs from `delta/own-extensions/<name>/`, or one side carries a file the other does not. | Extract the tree-side edit with `codkit save`, or bring the tree back to the delta with `codkit load`; the delta is the source of truth for an own extension. |
| `CK-E-TYPE-UNKNOWN` | The `type` of `codkit.json` is not in the registry of this codkit, or the package the registry names for it is not installed next to the tool. | Run `codkit types` for the identifiers this installation carries, and set `type` to one of them; if the identifier is right, install the package the row names. |
| `CK-E-TYPE-CAPABILITY` | The command needs an ability the declared project type does not have - brand images, the brand generator, the build channels, the runtime library - or `verify` was asked about an artifact of a layer that type does not provide. | Nothing was written. Use the verbs the type answers (`codkit types` prints the capability matrix), or move the artifact to a layer the type provides. |

## Warning codes

Warnings do not by themselves define the process exit status; read the surrounding command result.

| Code | Operator interpretation |
| --- | --- |
| `CK-W-MARK-RO` | A marker is being treated read-only in the reported context; review before expecting save/materialization to change it. |
| `CK-W-PATCHSET-SIDE-EDIT` | The patchset-side artifact changed while related tree work exists; reconcile both sources before continuing. |
| `CK-W-EMPTY-BLOCK` | A marker block contains no intervention content; remove it through the normal save flow or fill it intentionally. |

## Common operational traps

- Running `codkit --help`: help is currently the no-argument invocation; `--help` is an unknown flag and exits 2.
- Expecting `ci` to clone, fetch, pull LFS, install dependencies, or push: it does none of those. Prepare the Codkit installation, patch-set checkout, fork checkout, and caches first.
- Adding global `--ci` to `publish`: publication is a separate release-bot operation and deliberately rejects that combination.
- Treating `verify` exit 1 as a crash: it means the report completed and found violations. Read all findings from the same run.
- Editing a materialized overlay target or generated patch by hand: update the overlay source or edit inside the fork-tree marker and run `save`.

See the [command reference](commands.md), [conventions](conventions.md), and [CI examples](../ci-examples/README.md).
